definition: The process of breaking a complex, high-level goal into a series of smaller, more manageable subtasks.
details: Task decomposition is a core planning capability for agentic systems, allowing complex objectives to be tackled through a structured sequence of simpler, more verifiable steps rather than a single monolithic attempt.

explainer.lead: Task decomposition breaks a complex, high-level goal into smaller, more manageable subtasks. It matters as a core planning capability for agentic systems, replacing a single monolithic attempt with a structured sequence of simpler, more verifiable steps.

tiers.eli5: Like splitting a big chore into a checklist of small jobs you can tick off one at a time.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to structure agent planning so each step is simpler and more verifiable; the pitfall is that the decomposition itself must be sound for the sequence to succeed.
tiers.paperLevel: Breaking a complex, high-level goal into a series of smaller, more manageable subtasks; no formal definition or limit is given.

explainer.example: A high-level goal is split into an ordered list of subtasks that an agent executes and checks one by one.
